output_format_instructions.instruction: Unless the user specifies a format, default to generating BOTH pdf and docx for the resume and cover letter (the two most commonly requested by ATS systems and human reviewers). If the user names one or more specific formats, produce only those.

supported_formats.pdf: Final polished, print-ready output. Use consistent, ATS-friendly formatting: standard fonts (e.g., Calibri, Arial, Georgia), no text embedded in images/graphics, no tables/columns that break text extraction, no headers/footers containing content that should be machine-readable. This is the primary format for human reviewers and most ATS uploads.
supported_formats.docx: Editable Word document mirroring the pdf content and section order exactly, so the person can hand-tweak wording before submission. Same ATS-friendly constraints as pdf apply (no text-in-images, avoid complex tables).
supported_formats.txt: Plain text, no styling, section headers as plain capitalized lines (e.g., 'WORK EXPERIENCE'), single-column, no tables or special characters -- for ATS portals that only accept plain text paste/upload, or for pasting into an online application form field.
supported_formats.md: Markdown version using standard headers (#, ##), bullet lists (-), and bold (**text**) for section titles and job titles/companies. Useful for hosting on the djdole GitHub profile repo (e.g. as an alternate resume view or linked doc) and for version-control-friendly diffing between tailored versions.
supported_formats.json: A structured, tailored subset of this knowledge base reflecting the choices made for this specific JD -- i.e. NOT the full knowledge base, but the resolved output: chosen summary, reordered/selected skills, chosen work_experience bullets per role, and the generated cover letter text. Useful for the user to archive exactly what was submitted to a given employer, or to feed into another downstream tool. Should be valid, well-formed JSON.

output_format_instructions.consistency_rule: All requested formats for a given generation request must contain identical substantive content (same summary, same selected bullets, same skills, same cover letter body) -- formats differ only in styling/structure/markup, never in which facts or bullets were chosen. Generate the content decisions once, then render into each requested format.

generation_workflow_for_llm: 0. Determine JD input type: if the user provides a URL to a job posting, fetch/retrieve the page content first and extract the job description text from it (ignore surrounding site chrome, nav menus, 'similar jobs' widgets, etc. -- use only the actual posting content: title, company, responsibilities, requirements). If the page cannot be retrieved (paywalled, login-gated, JS-rendered with no visible text, link broken/expired), tell the user the page could not be read and ask them to paste the JD text directly rather than guessing at its contents. If the user pastes JD text directly, use it as-is. If no JD or link is provided at all, treat this as a generic/no-JD request: use summary_variants as-is, default skill ordering, all default bullets, and cover_letter_building_blocks.generic_fallback_template.

1. Parse the job description (JD) for: role title, key required skills/tools, years of experience required, role type (SDE/SDET/hybrid), company name, and any standout keywords (e.g., 'Kubernetes', 'webhooks', 'mentoring', 'on-call').
2. Choose title framing: use 'title_by_variant.SDE' or 'title_by_variant.SDET' per work_experience entry based on detected role type from meta.output_rules.role_detection_hints.
3. Choose or synthesize the summary using summary_variants or summary_building_blocks, weaving in 2-3 JD keywords that are truthfully supported by this knowledge base.
4. Reorder the 'skills' object's categories so categories matching JD keywords appear first in the rendered resume.

5. For each work_experience entry, select the bullet variant (e.g., '_sde_variant' vs '_sdet_variant' vs default) that best matches the detected role type; where no variant exists, use the default bullet text possibly lightly reworded (not fabricated) to echo JD phrasing.

6. Prioritize including bullets whose 'themes' or 'skills' arrays overlap with JD keywords; it's acceptable to omit lower-relevance bullets for space, but never omit an entire employer/role from the timeline (maintain full chronology/continuity for ATS and recruiter trust).

7. Keep all dates, employer names, and job titles exactly as given; never invent metrics (e.g., percentages, dollar amounts) not present in this file. Never use an em dash in any generated or reworded text; see meta.output_rules.never_use_em_dash.

8. For the cover letter, select body_paragraph_themes matching the JD's role type/emphasis, and personalize opening_hook_options and closing_options with the actual company name and role title from the JD. If no JD/company is provided, use cover_letter_building_blocks.generic_fallback_template as-is instead of synthesizing a new one.
9. Output should clearly separate RESUME and COVER LETTER content unless the user asks for only one.

10. If the JD was fetched from a URL, briefly note at the top of the output which company/role was detected from the posting, so the user can quickly confirm the right JD was used before reading the full output.

11. Determine requested output format(s) per output_format_instructions: default to pdf + docx if the user doesn't specify; honor explicit format requests (docx, json, md, pdf, txt, or any combination). Make the content decisions (summary, skills order, bullets, cover letter text) exactly once, then render that identical content into each requested format per output_format_instructions.consistency_rule.
